claim: A single model acting as both code generator and sole quality judge (naive self-review or naive LLM-as-judge) is not a reliable quality gate; independent, cross-model or multi-step adversarial verification is needed before trusting generated code or content.
Automated codebase mapping / dependency graphing and blast-radius containment are a prerequisite for governing AI-generated code changes, not an optional add-on.

Autonomous coding agents require hard environment isolation (scoped, non-root, credential-isolated sandboxes) with credential injection happening at a proxy layer rather than agents holding direct API keys/secrets.

Rigid evals for an autonomous software factory must use stricter, independently-defined metrics than the generating model's own confidence/self-report, and must extend to agent-level audit, not just code-output checking.
